title: Signal loss recovery in ELISA analysis of amyloid-beta via novel sample pre-treatment
author: Janssen, Sobott, et al.
materials: •Thaw hemi-forebrains on ice.•Add 500 μl of ice-cold TNT-buffer [50 mM Tris-base (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% Triton X-100, 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF), 2 mM 1,10-phenanthroline monohydrate (Merck Millipore), 1× protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma–Aldrich), pH 7.40].•Dissociate tissue with a 1-ml syringe (three aspirations without a needle and five aspirations with a 20-gauge needle).•Dissociated further by pipetting up and down 8–10 times with a 1-ml pipette.•Centrifuge at 18,000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C.•Collect the supernatant and centrifuge a second time at 18,000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C.•Collect the supernatant of this second centrifugation step and store at −20 °C. This supernatant contains the fraction of soluble proteins (SP).•Resuspend the pellet of the first centrifugation step in 750 μl RIPA-buffer [50 mM Tris-base (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 150 mM NaCl, 0.5% Triton X-100, 1 mM ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, 3% SDS, 1% deoxycholate, 1 mM PMSF, 2 mM 1,10-phenanthroline monohydrate (Merck Millipore), 1× protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma–Aldrich), pH 7.40].•Vigorously dissociate 20 times with a 1-ml pipette.•Vortex 20 s.•Placed on an overhead shaker (Heidolph) for 15 min at 4 °C.•Centrifuge at 18,000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C.•Collect supernatant and centrifuge a second time at 18,000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C.•Collect the supernatant and store at −20 °C. This supernatant contains the fraction of membrane-bound proteins.

•Dry samples in a Savant™ SpeedVac™ concentrator (Thermo Fisher Scientific).•Reconstitute in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), TFA, HFIP or FA.•Place samples in a sonication bath for 15 min.•Remove TFA and HFIP by drying under a constant stream of nitrogen gas.

steps.title: Thaw and buffer brain tissue
steps.instruction: Place hemi‑forebrain samples on ice until thawed, then add 500 µl ice‑cold TNT‑buffer (50 mM Tris‑base, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1 % Triton X‑100, 1 mM PMSF, 2 mM 1,10‑phenanthroline monohydrate, 1× protease inhibitor cocktail, pH 7.40).

steps.title: Mechanically dissociate tissue
steps.instruction: Using a 1‑ml syringe, aspirate the suspension three times without a needle and five times with a 20‑gauge needle, then pipette up‑and‑down 8–10 times with a 1‑ml pipette.

steps.title: First high‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 18 000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect soluble protein supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a new tube, repeat the centrifugation at 18 000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C, collect the second supernatant (soluble protein fraction) and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in RIPA buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet from the first centrifugation in 750 µl RIPA‑buffer (50 mM Tris‑base, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 % Triton X‑100, 1 mM EDTA, 3 % SDS, 1 % deoxycholate, 1 mM PMSF, 2 mM 1,10‑phenanthroline monohydrate, 1× protease inhibitor cocktail, pH 7.40).

steps.title: Further dissociation and shaking
steps.instruction: Vigorously pipette the suspension 20 times with a 1‑ml pipette, vortex for 20 s, then place on an overhead shaker (Heidolph) for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Second high‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 18 000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect membrane protein supernatant (optional)
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant, repeat the centrifugation at 18 000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C, collect the second supernatant (membrane‑bound protein fraction) and store at –20 °C. (For this study only the soluble‑protein fraction is used.)

steps.title: Dry soluble protein samples
steps.instruction: Place the soluble‑protein aliquots in a Savant™ SpeedVac™ concentrator (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and dry completely.

steps.title: Reconstitute in selected chemical
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each dried sample in 1 × the original volume of either phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS), trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), hexafluoro‑isopropanol (HFIP) or formic acid (FA).

steps.title: Sonicate samples
steps.instruction: Place the reconstituted tubes in a sonication bath for 15 min.

steps.title: Remove volatile chemicals
steps.instruction: If TFA or HFIP was used, evaporate the solvent by drying under a constant stream of nitrogen gas. If FA or PBS was used, perform a second run in the SpeedVac to remove the liquid.

steps.title: Final reconstitution before ELISA
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried residues in the final analysis buffer—ultrapure water, PBS or 1 % NH₄OH—immediately before ELISA measurement.

steps.title: Dilute to assay range
steps.instruction: Sequentially dilute the sample after each reconstitution step so that the final concentration falls within the measurement range of the ELISA kit.

description: Oligomerization of amyloid-beta (Aβ) can lead to epitope masking and steric hindrance, which can result in an underestimation of the Aβ concentration in ELISA analysis (Fig. 1). We, therefore, decided to develop a chemical pre-treatment protocol to disaggregate Aβ oligomers in samples prior to analysis. Three candidate chemicals with disaggregation properties, namely trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) [1], hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) [2] and formic acid (FA) [3] were selected from literature and applied to various samples to evaluate efficacy of the protocol and to identify the most promising option for future research. First, the pre-treatment protocol was tested with synthetic Aβ monomer solutions to assess any unwanted effects. Next, we progressed to solutions of aggregated synthetic Aβ to determine the efficiency of the various treatments. Finally, we examined the compatibility of the protocol with biological samples, i.e., brain extract of the APP23 mouse model for AD and cerebrospinal fluid from human AD patients and control individuals. Initially, we investigated whether the chemical treatments had any unwanted effects on the ELISA measurement of Aβ by subjecting our standard solution of synthetic Aβ 1-40 monomers (0.1 ng/ml) to the various treatments. ELISA results indicated significant, unwanted effects in some treatment groups (F4,37 = 42.813; p < 0.0001; Fig. 2). Post-hoc Bonferroni tests between the individual groups showed there was no significant difference between measurements of untreated standard and TFA-treated (p = 0.884) or FA-treated (p = 0.231) standard. On average, these three groups showed minimal deviation (<10%) from the theoretical standard concentration, demonstrating no adverse effect of these sample pre-treatments on sample recovery. The control group, treated with PBS, and the HFIP-treated group did appear to experience a significant reduction in signal due to the procedure, when compared to the untreated group (both p < 0.0001; Fig. 2).
